text.p: Salomon Brothers in London initiated Polish brewer Zywiec SA with an "underperform" rating, noting the firm's weak performance in 1996 and that only a partial recovery was expected this year.
Salomon said in a February 24 report Zywiec was trading at 47 times Salomon's 1997 forecast earnings, a 160 percent premium to the market and said it believed the premium was unjustified.
"In our view Zywiec's dim prospects of better financial results in the foreseeable future do not bode well for investors and we rate the stock underperform," it said. @

Salom saw Zywiec's net income rising to 12.3 million zlotys this year and to 20.2 million in 1998, from 8.1 million in 1996, but said the forecasted net was still lower than 1995 net of 27.1 million zlotys and 21.1 million earned in 1994.
It expected the brewer's total revenues to rise to 465.7 million in 1997 and to 573.8 million in 1998, from 368 million in 1996.
It added, however, that any increased involvement by Zywiec strategic partner Heineken would be likely to boost the share price. On Tuesday Zywiec closed at 192 zlotys.
